thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT: realtime-latency-detector detected sustained p99 latency > 2.2s for /v1/generate (5m) — rolling alert. Auto-escalation to oncall. :rotating_light:

alex: seeing it on the dashboard too. p95 jumped to ~1.1s, p99 spiking to 2.3-2.6s. Streaming stalls for a subset of requests.

maria: confirmed. Topology: mostly eu-west-1, model variant: redwood/llama-3-13b-q4.

kevin: any recent deploys? I don't see related release notes in the last 30m.

jess: no deploys from infra team. I pulled traces — tail latency correlates with backend GPU queue depth rising on pool gpu-infer-eu-2.

alex: paging infra oncall (pager-duty). tagging @pager-duty — can you confirm cluster health and autoscaler?

pager-duty: Oncall acked. Looking at cluster, nodes look healthy but kube-sched shows increased pending pods for autoscale group. Possible control-plane throttle.

maria: quick impact check: bounded requests failing? I see elevated 504s ~0.6% in last 5m, mostly long-stream timeouts. Customers hitting streaming endpoints.

kevin: add quick mitigation: set routing policy for /v1/generate to fallback model redwood/llama-3-7b-q4 for non-critical traffic and drain new sessions off the affected GPU pool. Patch applied in routing service.

alex: leaving a note so SRE can roll back if needed. action: set fallback routing -> executed.

ops-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: traffic split changed: primary->gpu-infer-eu-2 (70%), fallback->gpu-infer-eu-1 (30%) with model override redwood/llama-3-7b-q4.

jess: good. also increasing concurrent workers on healthy nodes to absorb bursts: `kubectl scale deployment inference-workers -n inference --replicas=40`

maria: I'm running quick checks on KV cache pressure and prefix cache hit ratio. If cache churn is high we might see stalls for cold prefixes.

kevin: check streaming proxy errors. Run:
```
kubectl logs -l app=stream-proxy -n inference --since=10m | grep "partial_stream_error" | wc -l
```

alex: results: ~120 partial_stream_error in last 10m. proxy returning 502 for some backpressure scenarios.

maria: hypothesis: a combination of autoscaler jitter + kernel saturation on that GPU pool causing long scheduling waits -> backlog -> proxy timeouts.

jess: short-term mitigation: extend streaming proxy timeouts from 20s -> 40s for EU region so clients don't cut off while we scale. Pushing config now.

ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: stream-proxy timeout EU increased to 40s.

pager-duty: autoscaler alert: API rate-limited for scale-up requests, manual bumping node group desired count to speed up. Executing now.

kevin: while nodes come up, we should temporarily limit large-context requests to the model variant to reduce queue length. Add request-size guard for >2048 tokens to 429 for the affected model.

alex: PR for guard in edge router created and hot-fixed to prod.

maria: dashboards: p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 1.4s after routing shift and timeout increase. p95 back to ~0.9s. Still monitoring for regressions.

jess: customers: support-cases flagged 3 customers with degraded streaming. I posted the incident note to the support thread and asked for customer-specific mitigation (retry guidance).

kevin: runbook tick-list: (1) confirm no deploys (done), (2) apply routing fallback (done), (3) bump nodes (in progress), (4) extend proxy timeout (done), (5) apply token-limit guard (done), (6) monitor for 15m stable.

alex: good running log. assigning incident lead to alex for the next handoff window. Oncall rotation, please prepare formal incident doc if still unstable at next check-in.

pager-duty: nodes scaled +6 in auto group, new nodes ready. kube pending pods cleared.

maria: monitoring: p99 trending down to 1.1s and errors dropped to 0.15%. Streaming stalls reduced. Looks like primary mitigations working.

jess: note: we should follow up with infra to investigate autoscaler API throttling and consider raising scaling limits or rate-limiting scale requests.

kevin: agree. Also flag model variant performance — 13b quantized variant shows larger tail under high concurrent loads. Add to post-incident action items: perf test 13b q4 under realistic bursty traffic.

alex: closing loop: current severity -> SEV3 (degraded streaming with partial customer impact). Containment achieved. We'll keep thread open for 1h to monitor and then write a postmortem if root cause deeper than autoscale throttle.

maria: thanks all. leaving final checks for 15m. :white_check_mark:
